Multinomial logistic regression analysis was performed to examine factors associated with trajectory class membership. A total of 2457 healthcare workers who completed all four surveys were included. Three distinct burnout trajectories were identified: recovery trajectory (41.3%), stable burnout trajectory (33.0%), and delayed elevations trajectory (25.7%). Traumatic event exposure was associated with increased odds of both the stable burnout (OR = 1.476) and delayed elevations (OR = 1.465) trajectories and occupational exposure with both the stable burnout (OR = 1.640) and, more strongly, the delayed elevations (OR = 4.487) trajectories. Good sleep quality (stable burnout: OR = 0.642; delayed elevations: OR = 0.440), an adequate sleep duration of 6-8 h/day (stable burnout: OR = 0.746; delayed elevations: OR = 0.545), and, for the delayed elevations trajectory, regular exercise (OR = 0.645) were associated with lower odds of the adverse trajectories. The developmental trajectory of occupational burnout among healthcare professionals exhibits significant heterogeneity, necessitating the development of tailored interventions for specific subgroups to ensure workforce stability. Healthcare administrators should implement trajectory-specific interventions. Given the strong associations of traumatic event exposure and occupational exposure with the adverse trajectories, trauma-informed care and workplace support, alongside the promotion of adequate sleep and regular physical activity, should be priorities. Because these recommendations are based on observational data, they warrant evaluation in interventional research.

papers.title: [Mitochondrial regulation in spaceflight environment-induced stress injury: recent research advances].
papers.abstract: With the continuous development of manned spaceflight in deep-space exploration, astronauts are chronically exposed to extreme space environments including microgravity, cosmic radiation and circadian rhythm disorder. These environmental factors can induce systemic stress injuries such as cardiovascular remodeling, skeletal muscle atrophy, immune dysfunction and oxidative stress, which cause adverse threats to astronauts' health and mission safety. Recently, multi-omics studies have demonstrated that mitochondria, as the central hub of cellular energy metabolism and a key regulator of cellular stress response, play a critical role in spaceflight impact. In this review, we summarize the phenotypes of stress injury induced by extreme spaceflight environments, and analyze the underlying mitochondrial regulatory mechanisms including mitochondrial energy metabolism dysfunction, redox homeostasis imbalance, mitochondrial dynamic homeostasis disruption, and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis disorder. Furthermore, we try to explain the potential value of mitochondrial-targeted strategies, including mitochondria-targeted antioxidant intervention, mitochondrial function remodeling and mitochondrial dynamic regulation, in protecting against spaceflight injury. Finally, we prospect the future directions of mitochondrial-targeted strategies in aerospace medicine. This review aims to provide theoretical foundation and technical support for improving the health of orbit flight astronauts and optimizing protective protocols for deep space exploration.
papers.journal: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]

papers.title: Revealing Cu-Mn Electronic Structure in Activated CuMn/Al2O3 Catalyst By Decoupling of Overlapping X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Spectra.
papers.abstract: Mn-promoted Cu-based catalysts demonstrate high efficiency and stability in various chemical processes, including methanol synthesis. XPS investigations of catalytic reactions and active catalytic centers in Cu-Mn-based catalysts face certain problems: it is challenging to determine the Mn oxidation state because of the strong overlap of Cu and Mn photoelectron and Auger spectra. In this study, a strict background subtraction based on a comprehensive set of standard samples as a reference was applied to separate the net Mn photoelectron spectra from the overlapping Cu signals, which reveals the Mn oxidation state with accurate quantitative analysis. Together with XAS, XRD, and HRTEM evidence, the results jointly support a strong Cu-Mn interaction and changes in their electronic states in the CuMn/Al2O3 catalyst during activation and passivation, providing new insights into the nature of the catalytic centers.

papers.title: Sleep, stasis, and thromboprotection: what hibernating mammals can teach us about cardiovascular risk.
papers.abstract: Prolonged immobility is one of the best-known triggers for venous blood clots, yet hibernating brown bears spend months lying still without ever developing them - and something similar seems to hold for many people with chronic paralysis. Thienel and colleagues recently offered a compelling explanation: platelets in hibernating bears sharply downregulate a protein called HSP47, dropping to roughly 55-fold below normal levels. HSP47 turns out to drive clot formation on two fronts at once, by boosting platelet activation and by prompting neutrophils to release the web-like structures that help clots take hold. Suppress it, and both arms of the process weaken together. That this pattern shows up across bears, immobilized patients, bed-rest volunteers, and other animal models suggests it isn't a quirk of bear physiology but something closer to an ancient survival mechanism. Here we consider why immobility's clotting risk seems to shift over time, look at an HSP47-blocking compound called Col003 that is already showing promise, and ask whether HSP47 might eventually double as a marker of clotting and inflammatory risk more broadly.

papers.title: Associations of Diet, Alcohol Consumption, Physical Activity, and Sleep With Functional Decline or Death Among Early Older Adults in Japan: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Large-Scale Medical and Long-Term Care Claims Data.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the associations between overall lifestyle patterns and functional decline in early older adults. We used medical claims, annual health checkup, and long-term care insurance claims data from one prefecture in Japan. Participants were independent adults aged 65-74 years who had undergone a health checkup in fiscal year 2020. Latent class analyses were conducted separately for males and females using lifestyle-related variables from the checkup questionnaire-specifically, smoking, regular exercise, walking habits and speed, mastication, eating speed, late-night dinner, snacking frequency, skipping breakfast, drinking frequency and amount, and sleep. The composite outcome, defined as the transition to care needs level ≥ 1 or death, was compared across latent lifestyle classes using survival analysis. A total of 15 818 participants (mean age: 69.7 years; women: 59%) were included. The median follow-up period was 1065 days for males and 1075 days for females. Five latent lifestyle classes were selected for each sex. Among males, the latent class characterized by low alcohol consumption, physical inactivity, poor mastication, and poor sleep showed a higher risk of functional decline or death than the occasional drinking, high-physical activity class (hazard ratio: 2.39, 95% confidence interval: 1.45-3.94). No significant differences were observed among the five latent lifestyle classes in females. The latent lifestyle pattern characterized by low alcohol consumption, physical inactivity, poor mastication, and poor sleep was associated with a higher risk of functional decline or death in independent males aged 65-74 years.

papers.title: Temporal spectroscopy of plant development reveals subcircadian response bands.
papers.abstract: Biological development is governed by internal clocks and feedback processes with characteristic response times. While circadian (∼24 h) and ultradian (∼hours) rhythms are well established, the existence and functional relevance of regulatory processes operating on characteristic subcircadian timescales remain largely unexplored. Here we treat a living organism as a driven dynamical system and introduce a temporal spectroscopy approach to probe its intrinsic regulatory timescales. Using Arabidopsis thaliana as a model system, we apply square-wave light-dark forcing with systematically varied periods spanning 5 s to 5400 s, while conserving the total daily photon dose. The organismal response is strongly nonmonotonic in forcing period and reveals three discrete, highly responsive frequency bands centered on seconds (10.5-42 s), minutes (168-336 s), and hours (1350-5400 s). Forcing within these bands induces sharp transitions in morphology and life-history trajectories, including programmable reallocation of growth between root and shoot systems, suppression of lateral root emergence, and frequency-dependent extension of lifespan by up to 60% without loss of final biomass. These responses are not consistent with simple photon integration or stress accumulation, but instead are consistent with a hypothesis of frequency-selective coupling between external forcing and internal regulatory processes. The characteristic frequencies align with known kinetic timescales of ion fluxes, membrane potential dynamics, photoreceptor signaling, metabolic turnover, and circadian gating, suggesting a hierarchical architecture of biological timescales. Our results uncover a temporal structure underlying development and establish frequency as an independent physical control parameter for reprogramming biological systems. More broadly, this work demonstrates that oscillatory environmental forcing can be used as a discovery tool to map the internal timescales governing complex living matter.

papers.title: The electrochemical physiology of organelles.
papers.abstract: Membrane-bound organelles maintain distinct chemical environments that are essential for their specialized functions. Yet, while organelle morphology, protein composition and dynamics have been extensively characterized, very little was known about their lumenal microenvironment prior to work from our laboratory. Here, we chart the development of a chemical imaging approach that enabled the measurement of ions, reactive species and membrane potential within native organelles in living cells and organisms. These measurements reveal that organelles maintain characteristic ionic and electrical states, that populations of even a specific type of organelle can be chemically heterogeneous, and that lumenal ion levels change during organelle maturation or physiological events. Beyond simply defining the ionic milieu of organelle lumens, quantitative ion imaging revealed new ion transport mechanisms, demonstrated that cell surface ion channels are active in organelles, mapped reactive-species production at subcellular spatial resolution and linked organelle physiology to disease states and cellular behavior. Together, these findings reveal that organelles have electroal behaviour because they harbor transmembrane ion gradients, ion transporting proteins, and membrane potential. We discuss how this emerging view may illuminate inside-out signaling across organelle membranes and outline the technological advances required to move from static chemical maps toward real-time, single-organelle physiology in living systems.

papers.title: The Histone Acetyltransferases Tip60 and CBP Differentially Regulate Alcohol-Induced Neuroadaptations in Drosophila Through the Ventrolateral Neurons.
papers.abstract: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic neuropsychiatric condition characterized by impaired control over drinking, persistent cravings, cognitive dysfunction, and sleep disturbances. Growing evidence suggests that many of these symptoms arise from alcohol-driven neuronal adaptations that promote tolerance and dependence, mediated in part by epigenetic reprogramming of the neuronal circuits that shape alcohol-related behaviors. Recent work in Drosophila implicates the PDF-expressing ventrolateral neurons (LNv) as key regulators of alcohol tolerance and alcohol-induced sleep disruption. However, the molecular mechanisms by which these neurons drive alcohol-evoked neuroadaptation remain unclear. Here, we test whether histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity in these circadian neurons is required for ethanol-induced tolerance and sleep phenotypes. We used the UAS-Gal4 and GeneSwitch systems to manipulate the expression of two HATs previously implicated in alcohol-induced neuroadaptation-Tip60 and CBP-with spatial and temporal precision. We measured ethanol sedation tolerance and quantified sleep/activity rhythms in genetically modified flies, analyzing sedation recovery time, total sleep, and circadian anticipation. Knockdown of Tip60 in LNv neurons abolished ethanol tolerance, whereas knockdown of nejire (CBP) in the same neurons enhanced ethanol tolerance. Similarly, Tip60 but not nejire knockdown reduced both daytime and nighttime sleep and prevented ethanol-induced sleep promotion. In contrast, knockdown of nejire disrupted the effects of ethanol on morning and evening anticipatory behavior, while Tip60 knockdown had no effect. Together, these results identify Tip60 and CBP as contrasting epigenetic regulators of alcohol-driven behavioral plasticity in Drosophila clock neurons.

papers.title: Effects of Lavender Essential Oil on People With Sleep Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses on lavender essential oil for sleep disorders have pooled heterogeneous routes of administration and clinical populations, and have not consistently applied contemporary risk-of-bias tools. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of lavender essential oil in adults with sleep disorders, with the primary analysis restricted to inhalation aromatherapy. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, WanFang, and VIP were searched from inception to September 22, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were eligible if they enrolled adults with primary sleep disorders or secondary/comorbid sleep disturbances, used lavender essential oil as an intervention, and reported sleep-related outcomes. The primary outcome was the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The primary meta-analysis was restricted to inhalation aromatherapy; oral, topical/massage, bathing, and mixed routes were examined in subgroup analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0. Random-effects models were used when heterogeneity was substantial. Subgroup analyses were performed by age, treatment duration, comparator, and route of administration. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots, Egger's test, and trim-and-fill analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. A total of 15 RCTs using inhalation aromatherapy were included in the primary analysis, and 5 RCTs using non-inhalation or mixed routes were included in subgroup analyses. Inhalation aromatherapy significantly improved PSQI scores compared with control [SMD = -1.14, 95% CI (-1.54, -0.74), p < 0.001; I2 = 88.2%]. Egger's test suggested potential publication bias (p = 0.012); however, trim-and-fill analysis did not identify any missing studies, and the pooled estimate remained unchanged. Subgroup analyses suggested that benefits may be greater in individuals aged ≥40 years and with treatment durations of 15-30 days. The certainty of evidence was [low/very low]. Inhalation aromatherapy with lavender essential oil may improve sleep quality in adults with sleep disorders, particularly in those aged ≥40 years and when used for 15-30 days. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity, risk of bias, and potential publication bias. Large, well-designed RCTs with standardized interventions and outcome measures are needed.

papers.title: Nightmare Engineering: Current State and Future Directions in Nightmare Treatment.
papers.abstract: Approximately, 85% of nightmare sufferers do not seek treatment and 70% of healthcare professionals have a substantial lack of knowledge how to treat nightmares. To improve patients' care, we propose several strategies, which can increase the incidence of patients seeking help, treatment efficiency and accessibility. First, we encourage stronger communicating strategies for accessible and feasible nightmare therapies. Second, within our concept of nightmare engineering, we present novel and tech-driven treatment methods against nightmares that may improve both accessibility and efficiency of treatment. Digital and app-based therapies offer location-independent, flexible and low-threshold self-guided therapy, incorporating structured elements of classical imagery rehearsal therapy (IRT) and cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT). With the current rise of artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs) open up the potential of human-like, individual-personalised and empathic-like conversations for nightmare treatment. Virtual reality (VR) technologies offer immersive realities for rescripting nightmares. Targeted memory reactivation (TMR) can reinforce and stabilise emotional rescripting elements by means of targeted sensory reactivation. Targeted lucidity reactivation (TLR) can be used to induce the state of lucid dreaming for promoting active control over nightmares by means of external stimuli via modern wearable technologies. Recent studies have shown preliminary efficacy of these potentially promising and future-oriented treatment methods, opening up new frontiers in nightmare engineering and nightmare treatment research. We critically discuss each treatment method in light of potential benefits, challenges and clinical relevance.

papers.title: Effect of Intraindividual Variability in Sleep on Long-Term Memory Encoding in Sleep-Restricted Individuals.
papers.abstract: Greater variability in sleep across nights is generally associated with poorer cognitive outcomes, but some recent evidence suggests that for sleep-restricted individuals, a variable sleep schedule that allows for prophylactic and/or recovery sleep might lessen impairment in some basic cognitive functions compared to a stable schedule. This study examined whether multiple nights of sleep restriction with consistent or variable sleep duration affected declarative memory encoding differently. After two baseline nights of 8-h time-in-bed (TIB), 44 participants (21-26 years, 20 males) underwent five manipulation nights with one of three sleep schedules: 8-h TIB per night (control group), 6-h TIB per night (stable short sleep group) or 8-4-8-4-6 h TIB (variable short sleep group). A picture encoding task was administered after the fifth manipulation night, and memory performance was assessed in a recognition test after two recovery nights of 8-h TIB. Compared to the control group, the variable short sleep group exhibited poorer memory performance, characterised by a greater tendency towards 'unsure' responses for both old and new pictures (p = 0.05; p = 0.09). In contrast, the stable short sleep group did not show significant impairment in memory performance, but instead showed more correct rejections (p = 0.04). These findings suggest that among sleep-restricted individuals whose sleep duration varies substantially across nights, declarative memory may be encoded with reduced strength, thereby increasing response uncertainty at retrieval even after recovery sleep. Minimising sleep variability may optimise declarative memory encoding in sleep-restricted persons. Trial Registration: NCT04731662.

papers.title: CSF Biomarkers of Synaptic Damage and Dysfunction in Epilepsy and Epileptic Seizures.
papers.abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is considered a key mechanism in epileptic seizures (ES), but no biomarkers are available to date to track its progression. We investigated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) synaptic proteins (beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, neurogranin) in a well-characterized cohort of patients with epilepsy and ES. We measured CSF concentrations of several markers (beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, and neurogranin, as well as of two other biomarkers, namely, neurofilament light chain, NfL, and glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP) in a single-centered prospective cohort. Study population included 20 patients with unprovoked or acute symptomatic ES, 50 patients with epilepsy from the outpatient clinic, and 36 disease controls. In 60 patients, CSF samples were collected after recent ES (median time: 3 days, IQR: 2-5), whereas in 10 patients with epilepsy during ES-free intervals (i.e., last ES >3 months before CSF analysis). CSF concentrations of beta-synuclein (p = 0.02), NfL (p<0.001), and GFAP (p<0.001) were significantly higher in patients after recent ES than in controls, especially in patients with ES of structural etiology and in patients with CSF pleocytosis (cell count >4 cells/µL). CSF NfL (p = 0.012) and GFAP (p = 0.022) were also elevated in patients with epilepsy assessed in ES-free periods. CSF SNAP-25 and neurogranin did not significantly differ between patients' and control groups. CSF biomarker levels were not significantly associated with epileptic potentials at electroencephalography, antiseizure therapy, ES semiology, status epilepticus, and ES recurrence at 6-month follow-up. CSF analysis showed evidence of synaptic, neuroaxonal, and astroglial injury after ES, and chronic neuroaxonal and astroglial dysfunction in ES-free patients with epilepsy.

papers.title: Time of day as an unmeasured dimension of lisdexamfetamine efficacy in binge-eating disorder.
papers.abstract: Lisdexamfetamine (LDX) is approved in the United States for moderate-to-severe binge-eating disorder (BED) in adults. Its efficacy was established on aggregate endpoints, chiefly binge days per week. Binge eating is not evenly distributed across the day: momentary-assessment studies place the highest risk of an episode in the late afternoon and more severe loss of control in the evening. Whether a once-daily morning dose controls symptoms in those hours has not, to our knowledge, been tested. By temporal coverage we mean the maintenance of the drug's effect on binge episodes and their proximal drivers, craving and loss of control, at each time of day. We do not claim that drug exposure wanes by the evening. The gap concerns measurement, because the trials that established efficacy did not report when episodes occurred. Evening episodes during treatment could also reflect the disorder's own evening weighting, daytime undereating, sleep disruption, or waning efficacy with prolonged use, and the timing of residual episodes alone cannot separate these from weaker evening coverage. We specify the analysis that could separate them, a treatment-by-time-of-day interaction comparing the reduction in episodes against placebo and baseline at each time of day. Recording the clock time of binge episodes would allow this test, and an estimate of how often evening breakthrough occurs.

papers.title: Smartphone addiction, social media use, and nomophobia among Turkish nursing students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Problematic smartphone use is a growing behavioral health concern among university students. Nomophobia, defined as anxiety or discomfort when mobile phone access is unavailable, may indicate technology-related psychological vulnerability. Nursing students may be particularly vulnerable due to academic demands, frequent smartphone use, and reliance on digital communication. However, the relationship between smartphone addiction, nomophobia, and their predictors requires further investigation in this population. This study aimed to examine the relationship between smartphone addiction and nomophobia and to identify significant predictors of nomophobia among Turkish nursing students. This cross-sectional correlational study was conducted with 296 undergraduate nursing students during the 2022-2023 academic year. Data were collected using a sociodemographic information form, the Smartphone Addiction Scale, and the Nomophobia Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Smartphone addiction was positively and moderately correlated with nomophobia (r = 0.544, p < 0.001). The multiple linear regression model was statistically significant and explained 47.0% of the variance in nomophobia scores (R²= 0.470). Higher smartphone addiction scores significantly predicted higher nomophobia levels (B = 1.109, β = 0.493, p < 0.001). Age (B = 2.107, β = 0.138, p < 0.05), monthly income (B = 0.002, β = 0.211, p < 0.001), daily sleep duration (B = 1.850, β = 0.094 p < 0.05), and specific social media usage characteristics (Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter) were also significant predictors of nomophobia. Structural equation modeling further supported this relationship, indicating that smartphone addiction positively and significantly predicted nomophobia (β = 0.62, p < 0.001) and explained 38% of its variance (R²= 0.38). Nomophobia was moderately associated with smartphone addiction among nursing students and may reflect a broader pattern of technology-related behavioral vulnerability. Early identification of problematic smartphone use and educational interventions addressing healthy smartphone habits may help reduce nomophobia and support students' well-being in nursing education settings.

papers.title: Social jet-lag, weekday-weekend differences in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, and depression in adolescents: a longitudinal cross-lagged study.
papers.abstract: Sleep and physical activity are two of substantial behavioral factors associated with adolescent mental health. Not only how much adolescents engage in health behaviors but also how regular these behaviors occur across time can affect their mental health. The present study used data from two large-scale mental health screenings among students in grades 5-12 conducted in NL county China, from October to November 2024 (T1) and in November 2025 (T2). We identified 25,941 students who participated in both waves for further analyses, yielding a follow-up rate of 90.36%. Cross-lagged panel models were applied to explore the longitudinal and potentially bidirectional associations between behavioral rhythm irregularities and depression among adolescents. Greater social jet-lag at T1 predicted increased depression at T2, whereas allocating a larger proportion of weekend time on moderate-to-vigorous physical activity predicted reduced depression. Conversely, depression at T1 was associated with greater social jet-lag and a reduced proportion of weekend time spent on moderate-to-vigorous physical activity at T2. Adolescents' behavioral rhythms are closely linked to depression. These findings suggest that sleep schedule regularity and weekend physical activity patterns may represent potential targets for future intervention research aimed at promoting adolescent mental health. Further studies, particularly intervention studies, are needed to establish the effectiveness of such approaches.

papers.title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of a transdiagnostic multidomain lifestyle intervention for psychiatric outpatients: feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effectiveness for improving recovery.
papers.abstract: People with mental illness often face psychosocial challenges, somatic comorbidities, and limited response to symptom-focused treatment, highlighting the need for effective recovery-oriented strategies. Lifestyle interventions are promising for improving recovery, but evidence on multidomain interventions in transdiagnostic samples is limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effectiveness of a transdiagnostic multidomain lifestyle intervention adapted for psychiatric outpatients. Forty-six outpatients were randomized (1:1) to receive the intervention (12 weekly group sessions + 3 follow-up sessions) or treatment-as-usual. The intervention targeted multiple lifestyle domains: physical activity, nutrition, relaxation, sleep, substance use, spirituality, social participation, and nature. Outcomes included feasibility (recruitment, retention, adherence), acceptability (participant evaluations, trainer feedback) and preliminary exploratory effectiveness (self-report questionnaires and physical measurements on several recovery outcomes, including the Recovery Assessment Scale as primary effect measure). Outcomes were administered at baseline, post-intervention and follow-up. The intervention and research protocol appeared feasible and acceptable. This is reflected by relatively high intervention attendance (71%) and a low dropout rate (13%). Overall study retention was 83%. Participants rated the intervention 7.4/10 and particularly valued the topic relaxation and spirituality. The intervention content and its difficulty were reported as appropriate. The intervention appears suitable for real-world implementation in clinical practice, with minimal risks reported by trainers and participants. However, organizational factors such as staff capacity, high workload and organizational instability require attention. Exploratory analyses suggested positive trends across various recovery domains; notably on long-term for societal and personal recovery. However, effect estimates were imprecise (95% CI including zeros) and these exploratory findings should be interpreted with caution. Based on this pilot, inclusive multidomain lifestyle interventions in specialist mental healthcare appear feasible and well-received by a heterogeneous sample of mental illness. Results encourage further testing in a fully powered trial. This trial preregistered at 30-05-2023 at Overview of Medical Research in the Netherlands with trial registration number: NL-OMON53239, CCMO register number: NL83935.042.23.

papers.title: Preprocessing and feature extraction co-optimization for low-power EEG-based neurodegenerative disease detection: a benchmark on STM32 embedded platforms.
papers.abstract: Early differential diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) using electroencephalography (EEG) enables low-cost and non-invasive neurological monitoring. This study presents a lightweight TinyML framework for embedded EEG classification on resource-constrained microcontrollers. Twelve preprocessing techniques and six machine learning classifiers were evaluated on two public OpenNeuro datasets containing 88 participants. All pipelines were implemented on STM32 NUCLEO-64 and STM32WB55 platforms using INT8 quantization with CMSIS-NN. Results show that Sparse Decomposition combined with XGBoost achieved the best performance, reaching 94.46% accuracy and 92.1% sensitivity while requiring only 45 KB SRAM and low execution time, demonstrating the feasibility of wearable EEG diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for persistent feeding intolerance in critically ill patients: a prospective exploratory study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in improving persistent feeding intolerance (FI) in critically ill patients, with additional exploration of its effects on delirium and sleep. In this single-arm, open-label, prospective exploratory study, a large case series of 19 intensive care unit (ICU) patients with persistent FI received a standardized 3-day nasojejunal FMT as salvage therapy. FI improved in 89.5% (17/19) of patients, with a median time to improvement of 4 days. Enteral nutrition (EN) volume increased within 24 h after the first FMT compared with the preceding 24 h; however, the uncontrolled design precludes attribution of this temporal change to FMT alone. EN intake and prealbumin levels increased, while disease-severity scores (APACHE II and SOFA) and systemic inflammatory markers (CRP, NLR) decreased over follow-up. Microbiome analysis showed early compositional shifts, increased alpha diversity, changes in beta diversity, and detection of donor-associated taxa, including Bifidobacterium, Collinsella, Subdoligranulum, Bacteroides, and Megamonas, together with butyrate-producing Clostridia such as Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae. Immunological analysis revealed significant increases in CD8⁺ T cell and NK cell subsets. Delirium and sleep quality also improved significantly following FMT, with gut microbiota diversity positively correlated with sleep quality. Exacerbated fever occurred in 11/19 patients (57.9%), but only one patient had a temperature exceeding 38.5 ℃ during FMT; no severe organ dysfunction was attributed to FMT. This study provides preliminary evidence that FMT is feasible, has an acceptable safety profile, and may improve persistent FI in critically ill patients.

papers.title: The potential mediating role of social frailty in the associations of cognitive function, sleep duration, and life satisfaction with depressive symptoms in older adults: a cross-sectional study using CHARLS data.
papers.abstract: To examine the direct and indirect associations of cognitive function, life satisfaction, and sleep duration with depressive symptoms, with social frailty as a potential mediator, among older adults. Cross-sectional data from Wave 5 (2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; N = 4,491; aged ≥ 60 years) were analysed. Depression was measured using the CESD-10, cognitive function using a composite score (orientation, memory, and executive function), and social frailty as a sum of loneliness and social isolation scores. Hierarchical regression and structural equation modelling were conducted. The mean depression score was 16.97 (SD = 5.78). In hierarchical regression showed that life satisfaction (β = -0.265), cognitive function (β = -0.257), sleep duration (β = -0.174), health status (β = -0.156), social frailty (β = 0.113), and self-rated memory (β = -0.073) were significantly associated with depression symptoms, collectively accounting for 28.7% of variance. Path analysis further showed statistically significant indirect associations through social frailty linking life satisfaction, cognitive function, and sleep duration to depressive symptoms. These findings suggest a complex interplay among life satisfaction, social frailty, sleep duration, cognitive function, and depressive symptoms in older adults. Social frailty may serve as a potential intermediary pathway linking these factors to depression. As the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, longitudinal studies are needed to confirm directionality and evaluate whether interventions targeting social frailty can reduce depressive symptoms in ageing populations.

papers.title: Protocol-Aware Secondary Analysis of Archived NWB Current-Clamp Recordings: Feature Reportability, Stability, and Reproducibility.
papers.abstract: Reuse of archived electrophysiology data requires more than successful file parsing: measurements must also be supported by the protocol and acquisition structure from which they are derived. We developed a protocol-aware workflow for reproducible secondary analysis of intracellular current-clamp recordings stored in Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) format. The workflow performs exact acquisition-stimulus sweep pairing, technical-integrity quality control, protocol-family stratification, feature-specific computability and reportability assessment, sensitivity analysis, acquisition-sufficiency testing, and family-versus-pooled benchmarking while retaining data and code provenance. We evaluated the workflow on 177 independently identified marmoset cortical cells from DANDI:001776. All 9,651 candidate voltage-current records were exactly paired and passed the technical gates; 5,447 quality-controlled LongPulse sweeps formed 350 protocol families, of which 291 (83.1%) supported at least one primary-reportable feature. Endpoint reportability ranged from 48.9% to 63.7%. Passive cohort estimates were robust to tested analysis settings, whereas adaptation was more definition-sensitive and firing-rate-current slopes required broader current-level support. In multi-family cells, family-specific firing-rate-current slopes differed by more than 20% from pooled estimates in approximately 37% of eligible cells. These results show that NWB standardization alone does not establish analytical comparability. Explicit protocol context, reportability states, acquisition-sufficiency diagnostics, and provenance provide a reusable basis for auditable analysis and downstream computational modelling.

papers.title: The Role Of Sleep In The Incretin-Mimetic Pharmacological Treatment Of Overweight And Obesity.
papers.abstract: Long-acting glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists and related incretin-based obesity medications have transformed obesity treatment. However, variability in treatment response, gastrointestinal side effects, loss of skeletal muscle and bone mass, and weight regain following medication discontinuation remain important clinical challenges. Sleep health is increasingly recognized as a modifiable determinant of energy balance and weight regulation, yet its role in obesity pharmacotherapy remains largely unexplored. This narrative review summarizes evidence linking sleep health with obesity medication outcomes and examines potential mechanisms through which sleep may influence treatment response and long-term weight management. Emerging evidence suggests that adequate sleep duration and better sleep quality are associated with greater weight loss and improved weight loss maintenance during obesity treatment, although direct evidence in patients receiving obesity medications remains limited. Plausible pathways linking sleep with pharmacological treatment response include alterations in glucagon-like peptide - 1 physiology, energy intake and appetite regulation, physical activity, and body composition. Key research priorities include incorporating multidimensional sleep health assessments into obesity medication trials and testing whether sleep interventions can enhance behavioral and pharmacological treatment outcomes. Optimizing sleep health may represent a practical and modifiable behavioral target to enhance the effectiveness, durability, and personalization of obesity pharmacotherapy.

papers.title: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea: a multidimensional clinical framework for diagnosis and treatment-a narrative review.
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to provide an updated overview of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) across developmental stages and synthesize diagnostic and therapeutic evidence within a multidimensional clinical framework for individualized management. This paper provides a narrative review of current literature addressing pediatric OSA across its full clinical spectrum, including pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical presentation, diagnostic tools, and therapeutic options. Evidence from clinical trials, meta-analyses, and international guidelines was synthesized to highlight strengths and limitations of available strategies. Pediatric OSA encompasses potentially overlapping clinical profiles associated with adenotonsillar enlargement, nasal inflammation, obesity, craniofacial abnormalities, neuromuscular impairment, and syndromic conditions. These profiles inform a multidimensional clinical assessment integrating obstructive event frequency with gas exchange, symptoms, quality of life, anatomy, and comorbidities. Polysomnography remains the diagnostic reference standard. Treatment may combine surgery, medical therapy, positive airway pressure, orthodontic interventions, and weight management, although evidence certainty varies across interventions and outcomes. Upper-airway obstruction must be distinguished from hypoventilation requiring ventilatory assistance. The proposed multidimensional clinical framework integrates physiological and clinical characteristics to support phenotype-informed, individualized management, linking assessment to targeted or combined interventions and reassessment of persistent disease. • Pediatric OSA is a heterogeneous disorder whose clinical impact extends beyond sleep-related symptoms. • Diagnosis and treatment have traditionally relied on polysomnographic severity and adenotonsillar surgery. • This review proposes a multidimensional clinical framework integrating age-related features, symptoms, quality of life, gas exchange, anatomy, and comorbidities beyond the apnea-hypopnea index alone. • The framework supports individualized management by identifying predominant and coexisting contributors, informing targeted or combined treatment, and guiding reassessment of persistent OSA.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm disruption causes cognitive impairment through the basal forebrain-hippocampal cholinergic system.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is associated with cognitive impairments, yet the mechanisms involving cholinergic signaling remain elusive. This study investigated whether shift work alters cholinergic factors and impairs cognition through the basal forebrain-hippocampal pathway. In human subjects, we assessed cognitive performance using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and measured serum cholinergic biomarkers in shift workers and non-shift workers. In parallel, male C57BL/6 J mice subjected to circadian disruption were used to model shift-work-induced cognitive deficits, and male ChAT-IRES-Cre mice were employed for optogenetic interrogation of the basal forebrain-hippocampal cholinergic projection. Shift workers exhibited lower MoCA scores and altered cholinergic factor profiles compared with non-shift workers. In mice, circadian disruption caused cognitive impairment, reduced cholinergic neuron excitability, and disrupted synaptic transmission in the basal forebrain-hippocampal circuit. Optogenetic activation of this cholinergic pathway rescued cognitive performance in ChAT-IRES-Cre mice. These findings suggest that shift work-associated cognitive decline may involve cholinergic dysregulation, and that the basal forebrain-hippocampal cholinergic projection represents a potential circuit-level target for circadian-related cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Impact of circadian rhythm disruptions on the emotional brain: gray matter and functional connectivity changes in the amygdala.
papers.abstract: Acute circadian rhythm disruption (ACRD), increasingly prevalent in modern society due to chronic sleep disturbance and irregular sleep-wake patterns, has been linked to emotional dysregulation, including heightened susceptibility to depression and anxiety. Although the amygdala plays a critical role in emotional processing, the direct effects of ACRD on its morphology and function-and how these changes relate to sleep and affective disturbances-remain unclear. In this longitudinal study, healthy participants underwent 15 days of experimentally induced circadian rhythm disruption, which led to sleep and emotional disturbances. Questionnaire-based symptoms of the rhythm disorder restored by the 30-day follow-up. Ultra-high field (7 T) MRI scans were acquired before and after the intervention to assess morphology and functional changes in amygdala gray matter volume (GMV) and functional connectivity (FC). Our findings revealed a significant reduction in GMV within the left amygdala and its subregions-including the centromedial (CM), laterobasal (LB), and superficial (SF) nuclei-following ACRD. In contrast, no significant GMV changes were detected in the right amygdala or its corresponding subregions, suggesting a lateralized effect of ACRD. Moreover, GMV reductions in the left amygdala were significantly correlated with worsening scores on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Functional connectivity analysis demonstrated a nearly significant decrease in connectivity between the left medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and the left CM amygdala. Crucially, this work is the first to systematically investigate the neurobiological effects of ACRD on amygdala integrity and its implications for emotional regulation.

papers.title: Sleep as a window into thalamocortical pathology: generative modeling implicates NMDA receptor hypofunction in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
papers.abstract: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a strong genetic risk factor for neuropsychiatric conditions, including schizophrenia, yet the underlying synaptic mechanisms remain unclear. Sleep EEG suggests thalamocortical dysfunction, but scalp data alone lack mechanistic resolution. Computational modelling can bridge this gap by inferring receptor-level dynamics from EEG. We applied a conductance-based thalamocortical Dynamic Causal Model (DCM) to sleep-wake EEG from children with 22q11.2DS (n=28) and their neurotypical siblings (n=17), estimating contributions of AMPA, NMDA, GABAA, and GABAB conductances. Building on these estimates, we investigated which receptor systems, if perturbed, could shift circuit dynamics toward sibling patterns. To address this, we implemented in silico pharmacology by systematically scaling receptor-mediated conductances. Increasing NMDA receptor (NMDA-R) efficacy consistently produced the strongest improvements in alignment with sibling spectra (effect size = 0.32 in light NREM, 0.45 in deep NREM), whereas AMPA- or GABA-based manipulations were weaker. The most influential pathways were recurrent NMDA-R excitation among superficial pyramidal cells and NMDA-R excitation from spiny stellates to superficial pyramidal populations. Exploratory regressions linked greater thalamocortical delay during deep sleep to greater sleep problems (β=0.34, pFDR=0.006), and AMPA-mediated excitation of interneurons during wakefulness to anxiety symptoms (β=-0.32, pFDR=0.032). These findings implicate NMDA receptor hypofunction as a key mechanism in 22q11.2DS and suggest it may serve as a treatment target. We further show that DCM-based virtual pharmacology can simulate drug-level interventions, and we are now testing whether NMDA receptor modulation restores network activity in preclinical models (e.g., mouse models of 22q11.2DS).
authors: Marianne B M van den Bree

papers.title: Sleep Health Interventions Among Indigenous Peoples: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Given the disproportionate burden of sleep problems such as insomnia among Indigenous Peoples, we sought to examine the literature on sleep interventions in these populations. In this scoping review, we aimed to describe traditional Indigenous sleep improvement practices as well as non-Indigenous behavioral sleep interventions (e.g. cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, CBT-I) that have been adapted for and/or tested with Indigenous communities. We searched eight health sciences and Indigenous Peoples databases for articles that described or tested sleep health practices or interventions among Indigenous adolescents or adults located in North America, New Zealand, Australia or the Pacific Islands. Articles were screened and reviewed independently by two reviewers. Twenty articles met inclusion criteria. None described Indigenous-specific sleep practices. No articles focused on insomnia, and none mentioned CBT-I. Two articles described sleep health interventions with Indigenous Peoples. The remaining articles described recommendations for sleep health interventions based on their original research findings. This review underscores the limited published research on sleep health programs among Indigenous populations and the absence of insomnia-specific interventions, including CBT-I. The scarce literature possibly reflects a misalignment of the research questions and strategies with Indigenous views of sleep, rather than an absence of relevant knowledge. Overall, our findings highlight the need for approaches that address sleep health and insomnia among Indigenous populations. These approaches should be based on holistic frameworks nested in Indigenous worldviews that consider socio-economic inequities, community capacity, and culture.

papers.title: Warmer night-time temperatures are linked to poorer associative memory performance.
papers.abstract: Ambient temperature is emerging as an environmental factor that may influence cognitive performance in ageing populations. This is particularly relevant in Australia, where people live across diverse climatic regions spanning alpine to tropical conditions. We examined daily temperatures and cognitive performance in 1,873 midlife and older adults (1,297 women, mean age 61.0 years) who completed the Creyos online battery (formerly Cambridge Brain Sciences). Twelve tasks assessed memory, visuospatial processing, language, attention, and executive function. Task scores were linked to postcode-level contemporaneous weather data. The scores were analysed in relation to maximum and minimum air and wet-bulb temperatures and postcode- and month-relative temperature percentiles. Regression and distributed-lag models adjusted for age, sex, education, socioeconomic status, and climate zone, with season included for air and wet-bulb measures. Higher minimum, but not maximum, temperature was associated with poorer performance on Paired Associates, a task assessing associative memory. This pattern was observed for air temperature, wet-bulb temperature, and temperature percentile, suggesting poorer memory performance after warmer nights, both in absolute terms and relative to local seasonal norms. Associations were concentrated within a short-term window. Temperature was not significantly associated with performance on any other task, including measures of short-term/working memory, visuospatial processing, language, attention, or executive function. These findings suggest a task-specific association between higher overnight temperature and poorer associative memory performance, rather than a general reduction in cognition. Further studies incorporating personal exposure and sleep measures are needed to clarify whether night-time thermal conditions affect cognitive health in midlife and older populations.

papers.title: Hypothalamic orexin input to the medial amygdala promotes arousal from anaesthesia and modulates exploratory behaviour.
papers.abstract: Emergence from general anaesthesia is often accompanied by agitation, suggesting that recovery of consciousness can engage neural circuits that regulate arousal and behavioural responsiveness. The amygdala influences social, defensive, and exploratory behaviours, but whether orexinergic input to the amygdala regulates anaesthetic state transitions together with behavioural responses remains unclear. In male orexin-Cre mice, we combined viral tracing, electrophysiology, and RNAscope to define a lateral hypothalamic orexin (LHAOx) projection to the medial amygdala (MeA). Optogenetics, electroencephalography, electromyography, and fibre photometry were used to test how this circuit regulates arousal from isoflurane anaesthesia, as well as exploratory and place-preference behaviour. LHAOx neurones densely innervated the MeA, where orexin receptor 2 was more abundant than orexin receptor 1 (P<0.0001). Optogenetic activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection promoted arousal from 0.75 vol% isoflurane sedation (P<0.0001), delayed induction by 3 vol% isoflurane as measured by loss of the righting reflex (P=0.0074), and accelerated emergence from 2 vol% isoflurane as measured by return of the righting reflex (P=0.0098). In behavioural assays, activation of this projection suppressed open-field exploration, increased real-time place preference, and did not produce conditioned place preference. Activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection was accompanied by increased activity in MeA vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT)-expressing neurones. Direct activation of MeAvGAT neurones replicated the arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory behaviour, whereas silencing their synaptic output eliminated the induction-delaying effect and shifted the real-time preference. The LHAOx projection to the MeA promotes anaesthetic arousal and acutely suppresses exploratory behaviour in male mice, with MeAvGAT serving as a key downstream target.

papers.title: Cannabis Impairment and Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cells.
papers.abstract: Technologies to better determine impairment from cannabis use are essential. Understanding the functional losses that can occur with any use, medical or adult recreational use, will better assure the safety of individuals as well as the public. This study evaluated the Frequency Doubling Technology 710 (FDT710) tabletop field test as a screening tool for detecting retinal dysfunction associated with inhaled cannabis use. Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive component of cannabis, has been shown to impair dopaminergic dependent intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cell (ipRGC) functioning. These cells process non acuity functions; contrast, motion, depth, pupil response, and circadian rhythms. Participants were tested with the FDT710, which presented seventeen 10-degree targets across a 40-degree visual field and compared their results with the incorporated internal normative database. An opportunistic dosing protocol was used with self-dosing their own legally obtained cannabis at a location of their choosing. Fourteen volunteers completed consent procedures, blood draws, baseline undosed testing sessions, and research questionnaires. For the second visit, volunteers advised staff when and where they would be using their own cannabis products, and participants were transported by rideshare to the lab for post-use testing. Following acute cannabis use, the FDT710 demonstrated a moderate detection rate of 60% dysfunction, based on deviations from age-matched normative reference data. Significant changes from undosed performance were detected in six of the seventeen target areas. The ability to detect dysfunction in the visual system impairment following cannabis use is crucial for public health and safety for law enforcement.

papers.title: Health Behavior Classes Among Asian American Women: Associations With Discrimination, Sleep, and Mental Health.
papers.abstract: Health behaviors often cluster, but evidence on patterned behavioral risk among Asian American women remains limited. This study identified health behavior classes and examined discrimination-related correlates and class differences in sleep and health. Data came from a cross-sectional online survey of 356 Asian American women employed in Minnesota pink-collar occupations (September-October 2024). Workplace discrimination was assessed with a 14-item inventory, and lifetime gendered racial microaggressions were assessed with a 22-item scale. Latent class analysis considered five behavioral indicators: binge drinking, smoking, diet quality, exercise, and drug use. Class membership correlates were examined using corrected three-step multinomial models. Sleep quality, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and self-rated health were compared across classes using Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars auxiliary models. A three-class solution was retained: the Lower-risk (54.1%), Diet and activity risk (19.4%), and Substance-related risk (26.5%) classes. Higher gendered racial microaggression scores were associated with both risk classes relative to the Lower-risk class. Workplace discrimination was associated with the Substance-related risk class relative to both other classes. After adjustment for discrimination, both risk classes had poorer sleep and higher anxiety than the Lower-risk class; depressive symptoms were highest in the Substance-related risk class. Self-rated health was most favorable in the Lower-risk class and least favorable in the Diet and activity risk class. Asian American women in pink-collar work showed distinct behavioral risk patterns with different discrimination correlates and health burdens. Findings support class-tailored behavioral and mental health assessment alongside workplace efforts to reduce discriminatory exposures.
papers.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health

papers.title: Effect of a theory-informed multicomponent exercise program on cognitive function and other health outcomes among older adults with mild cognitive impairment: the MIND-STEP randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of the Motivational and INtegrateD peer-Interaction and Self-efficacy-enhancement mulTicomponent Exercise for Persons with MCI (MIND-STEP), a theory-informed multicomponent exercise program integrating peer interaction and self-efficacy enhancement, in improving cognitive and health outcomes among older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). In this single-blind, two-arm randomized controlled trial in nursing homes in Zhejiang, China, 156 participants were allocated 1:1 to a 12-week multicomponent exercise intervention based on the Health Action Process Approach and Theory of Planned Behavior, or usual care. Assessments were conducted at baseline and 6, 12, and 24 weeks. The primary outcome was change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Basic (MoCA-B) score from baseline to week 12. Compared with unstructured usual care, the MIND-STEP program significantly improved MoCA-B at 12 weeks (mean difference = 2.78; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.88 to 3.68, p < 0.001, standardized mean difference = 1.23; 95% CI: 0.83 to 1.63), with benefits observed at 6 weeks and maintained at 24 weeks. Intrinsic capacity, physical performance, depressive symptoms and sleep quality also improved. The MIND-STEP program improved cognition and overall health in nursing-home residents with MCI compared with unstructured usual care, supporting structured exercise and behavior-change strategies in routine nursing-home care.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: The Genetics of Sleep Regulation in Mice.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for health, yet the mechanisms that generate sleep states and encode the need for sleep are not yet fully understood. Mouse genetics has begun to transform these mechanisms into testable problems by linking specific genes and circuits to vigilance-state dynamics. Here, we review forward-genetic approaches that have uncovered unanticipated regulators as well as reverse-genetic strategies accelerated by CRISPR and adult brain-wide adeno-associated virus (AAV) perturbation. Recent work converges on phosphorylation-centered control of non-rapid-eye-movement sleep (NREMS), exemplified by the SIK3-HDAC4 pathway and related kinase-phosphatase networks. We discuss how neuromodulators orchestrate vigilance states through circuit- and receptor-dependent mechanisms and discuss emerging roles of ion channels, astrocytes, and microglia. Finally, we address methodological constraints in mouse sleep phenotyping and genetic manipulation that shape the interpretation of sleep phenotypes.

papers.title: Work-Related Fatigue Among Norwegian Anaesthesiologists With a Focus on Shift Work: A National Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.abstract: There is a growing focus on fatigue among anaesthesiologists; however, data on work-related fatigue in Norway, including its impact on personal well-being and the risks associated with driving home after night shifts, are limited. In this study, we aimed to assess working conditions, the perceived risk of driving home after night shifts, and the reported levels and effects of work-related fatigue among specialist and trainee anaesthesiologists in Norway. A cross-sectional, anonymous digital survey of specialist and trainee anaesthesiologists was conducted. These specialist and trainee anaesthesiologists were members of the Norwegian Association of Anaesthesia. A 27-item online survey was used to assess work-related fatigue and its impact on specialists and trainee anaesthesiologists. Ninety-five percent of the 408 specialist and trainee anaesthesiologists who responded reported having experienced work-related fatigue. The response rate was 22.5%. The lack of rest during shifts and understaffing were perceived as the most important contributing factors. Negative effects on health, sleep, and broader aspects of personal and social functioning were reported. Seventy-three percent of respondents have, at some point, been so fatigued at work that they considered it unsafe. Work-related fatigue is common among anaesthesiologists in Norway, with perceived impacts on patient safety and negative professional and personal consequences, including the risk of driving home. These findings warrant increased attention, and hospital management should implement fatigue risk management systems to address this issue. The results of this national survey highlights perceived fatigue among Norwegian anaesthesiologists, with reported consequences for wellbeing, patient safety, and driving after shifts. The low response rate and reliance on self-reported outcomes limit generalisability and causal interpretation. Nevertheless, these findings support greater organisational attention to staffing, rest opportunities, and fatigue management, alongside evaluation of interventions to improve clinician and patient safety.

papers.title: Translational neuroscience in psychoeducation: Mapping non-motor circuitry to clinical management in movement disorders.
papers.abstract: Non-motor symptoms (NMS) affect nearly all patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and related movement disorders, with a mean of roughly 8-10 discrete symptoms per individual. Their effect on quality of life often exceeds that of motor features, yet NMS remain under-recognized and undertreated, partly because patients and caregivers lack a working model of why these symptoms arise in a "movement" disease. This chapter applies neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) to that gap and positions it relative to conventional psychoeducation, health communication, and behavioral science. We propose the Map-Normalize-Differentiate-Navigate (MNDN) workflow as a movement-disorders-specific implementation of the NIPE framework described in Chapter 1 of this volume. MNDN is a clinical proposal, not a validated protocol: its components are specified so that it can be tested, but its effects on patient outcomes have not been evaluated. Drawing on the tripartite cortico-basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop model and multi-transmitter degeneration, we provide modules for seven high-yield NMS: apathy, anxiety, executive dysfunction, REM sleep behavior disorder, neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, psychosis, and fatigue. Each module summarizes the neural systems implicated, at the level of certainty the evidence supports, together with common misattributions, reversible contributors that must be excluded, management options and their limits, and patient and caregiver handout content. We describe delivery formats from 3 to 5 min "micro-NIPE" sessions in routine visits to group and telehealth programs, specify the minimum components, provider competencies, dose, fidelity criteria, and proximal outcomes needed to test MNDN, and examine the ethical risks of neurobiological framing (determinism, oversimplification, over-attribution, and false reassurance), with particular attention to prognostic counseling in REM sleep behavior disorder. NIPE in movement disorders is designed to reduce self-blame, support accurate symptom attribution, and improve collaborative management. Whether it does so is an empirical question that this chapter aims to make answerable.

papers.title: Fluorescence spectroscopy coupled with dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion for accurate quantification of microplastics in agricultural soils.
papers.abstract: Microplastic contamination in agricultural soils has emerged as a critical environmental issue, posing potential risks to soil ecosystems, food security, and human health. However, rapid and accurate quantification of soil microplastics remains challenging due to the limited sensitivity and feature extraction capability of conventional spectroscopic methods. To address these limitations, this study develops a fluorescence spectroscopy-based dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion (DM-CAFF) framework for the intelligent quantification of microplastics in agricultural soils. A total of 2400 fluorescence emission spectra were collected from soil samples containing different microplastic types, particle sizes, concentration levels, and soil backgrounds. First, to enhance spectral information representation, one-dimensional fluorescence spectra were transformed into improved two-dimensional gramian angular field (GAF) images, enabling the simultaneous characterization of local spectral variations and global distribution patterns. After that, variational autoencoder (VAE) and conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)-based augmentation strategies were employed to expand the dataset and improve sample diversity. Finally, a dual-modal learning framework was subsequently constructed to jointly exploit spectral sequence information and image-based spatial features. The proposed DM-CAFF framework achieved superior performance compared with conventional spectral analysis methods and existing fusion models, yielding a coefficient of determination for prediction (R2p) of 0.9757, root mean square error of prediction (RMSEp) of 0.4437 wt%, mean absolute error of prediction (MAEp) of 0.1173 wt%, and residual predictive deviation (RPDp) of 6.4147. In addition, excellent classification performance was obtained for seven categories of soil microplastics. The developed DM-CAFF framework provides a reliable technical reference for rapid quantitative detection of microplastics in agricultural soils.

papers.title: Sleep quality and its associations with psychological distress, pain and lifestyle factors in women with musculoskeletal pain recruited from municipal sports centres in Madrid, Spain: a cross-sectional study.
Clinical analysis of patients with refractory status epilepticus in a tertiary hospital in northern Ceará, Brazil: a case series.
papers.abstract: Refractory status epilepticus (RSE) is a neurological emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Despite its clinical significance, data from regional tertiary centers in Brazil remain limited. To characterize the clinical profile of RSE patients and to identify predictors associated with in-hospital mortality. In the current retrospective case series, we analyzed 21 patients hospitalized between 2023 and 2025 in a tertiary hospital in in the northern region of the state of Ceará, Brazil. Cases were identified via electroencephalography (EEG) screening and medical record review, following the diagnostic criteria of the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) for RSE. The mean age of the sample was 54.05 (median: 62) years, with 61.9% of female subjects. Hypertension (52.4%) and diabetes (28.6%) were the primary comorbidities. Depressed consciousness occurred in 76% of the cases. Prevalent metabolic disturbances included hypernatremia (85%) and metabolic acidosis (50%). The in-hospital mortality rate was 57.14%. The statistical analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between age and mortality (r = 0.72; p = 0.001). Notably, a significant negative correlation was found between overt motor seizures and death (r = -0.66; p < 0.001), with motor symptoms acting as a survival predictor (odds ratio [OR] = 31.50). In the cohort of the present study, RSE was associated with high lethality, especially in older patients. The inverse association between motor symptoms and mortality suggests that non-convulsive presentations delay diagnosis, leading to worse outcomes. These findings emphasize the urgent need for institutional protocols prioritizing continuous EEG monitoring and early therapeutic escalation in regional tertiary centers.

papers.title: [Predicting phenoconversion in prodromal Lewy body disease: machine learning models using multimodal neuroimaging data].
papers.abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a well-established prodromal marker of α-synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. However, the time to phenoconversion and the resulting clinical phenotype vary considerably among individuals. This review summarizes current neuroimaging biomarker research in iRBD and provides an overview of machine learning-based prediction models for phenoconversion, with a focus on their methodology, performance, and clinical applicability. Structural MRI studies have consistently identified gray matter volume reduction in subcortical structures and cortical thinning across frontal, temporal, and parieto-occipital regions, with several Cox regression analyses demonstrating their utility in phenoconversion risk stratification. Resting-state functional MRI has revealed disrupted connectivity within basal ganglia, cortico-striatal, and cortico-cortical networks, some of which correlate with cognitive and motor impairments. Notably, functional connectivity alterations are detectable even at early stages when structural changes remain subtle. Nuclear medicine studies, particularly dopamine transporter SPECT and cardiac metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy, provide complementary information on dopaminergic and autonomic denervation. Recent studies have applied machine learning algorithms to integrate these multimodal data, with preliminary evidence suggesting higher predictive performance than single-modality approaches. Machine learning models using clinical, electrophysiological, and neuroimaging features have demonstrated promising accuracy in predicting both the timing and subtype of phenoconversion. Nevertheless, several challenges must be addressed before clinical implementation: ensuring model explainability, elucidating patient heterogeneity through data-driven subtyping approaches, and validating models in prospective longitudinal cohorts. The clinical significance of prodromal prediction research is expected to grow in parallel with the development of disease-modifying therapies.

papers.title: Nonlinear association between daily rest period and psychological distress among Japanese public school teachers: a mixed-effects spline analysis.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the association between daily rest period (DRP) and psychological distress among Japanese public school teachers. Data were obtained from a nationwide survey conducted in 2022. After applying the eligibility criteria and complete-case analysis, 13,754 teachers were included. DRP was calculated as the average interval between the end of one workday and the start of the next across four weekday intervals. Psychological distress was assessed using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6). Linear mixed-effects models with school-level random intercepts were used. A natural cubic spline model examined the nonlinear association between DRP and K6 score, and sequentially adjusted models examined changes after adjustment for post-clock-out work, job stress, and total sleep time. Shorter DRP was associated with higher K6 scores. The spline model showed a better fit than the linear model and indicated that predicted K6 scores decreased as DRP increased, with the slope becoming more gradual around 13 h. Approximately 13 h was interpreted as a descriptive feature of the spline curve rather than as a statistically identified threshold. These findings suggest that avoiding shorter DRPs and securing sufficient post-work recovery time may be important for teachers' mental health.

papers.title: Associations of Prenatal Cannabis Exposure and Neonatal Brain Development in the HBCD Cohort.
papers.abstract: Prenatal cannabis exposure (PCE) is increasing in prevalence, yet its effects on brain development remain incompletely understood. We examined associations between maternal PCE and neonatal brain volumes and white matter microstructure and secondarily assessed the influence of prenatal nicotine exposure (PNE). This cohort study included 1,630 mother-infant dyads (222 with PCE) from the HEALthy Brain and Child Development Study. Maternal substance use was assessed using the Timeline Follow-Back method. Infants underwent natural-sleep T2-weighted structural and diffusion MRI within the first month of life. Analyses evaluated associations by exposure presence, gestational timing, and frequency among exposed infants. Secondary analyses examined PNE as a predictor and tested cannabis × nicotine interactions. PCE was associated with frequency-dependent increases in diffusivity values across white matter regions that remained significant after accounting for PNE. Timing-specific associations emerged, with first-trimester exposure linked to higher diffusivity values within cerebellar white matter regions and sustained exposure throughout pregnancy associated with higher diffusivity values within white matter association regions. In contrast, associations with subcortical brain volumes were attenuated after accounting for PNE, and significant PCE × PNE interactions across several subcortical regions suggested greater sensitivity of volumetric measures to nicotine co-exposure. Effect sizes were small for PCE presence and timing analyses and medium-to-large for PCE frequency analyses. These findings may reflect variation in early neurodevelopment rather than uniformly adverse effects and warrant longitudinal follow-up to determine their relationship with later clinical outcomes. Consideration of exposure timing, frequency, and co-occurring substance use may improve individualized counseling and developmental monitoring.
keywords: HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study

papers.title: Employing Microelectrode Arrays and Optogenetics to Interrogate Neural Networks in Neurodegenerative Disease Organoid Models.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction or loss and are traditionally mechanistically studied in vivo by applying a variety of non-human model systems. Human stem cell-derived 2D and 3D neuronal cultures and organoids are emerging as valuable complementary systems for in vitro modeling of human disease-relevant processes at molecular, cellular and network-levels as they increasingly offer more detailed, physiologically relevant context. The ability to genetically manipulate and rapidly scale these platforms for high-throughput analysis and drug screening makes them a vital component for advancing new therapeutic interventions. Perhaps the greatest accelerators of these neural stem cell technologies are functional interrogation tools such as microelectrode arrays (MEAs), optical electrophysiology, and optogenetic stimulation, which are transforming how neuronal activity is measured and manipulated in vitro. This review explores how emerging tools for measuring connectivity, excitability, and synaptic dynamics are integrated into high temporal and spatial-resolution studies to connect molecular pathology to systems-level behavior and drive therapeutic discovery in neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Modified Osteotomy Strategies for Severe Mandibular Retrognathism with OSAHS: A Proof-of-Concept Case Study.
papers.abstract: The study aimed to explore the biomechanical effects of different mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO) on the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), and evaluate its improvement on upper airway ventilation in severe mandibular retrognathism patients with OSAHS, via biomechanical analysis of the TMJ based on multimodal data fusion and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). One adult patient with skeletal Class II severe mandibular retrognathism and OSAHS was enrolled. CBCT and MRI data were collected to reconstruct the TMJ complex (including articular discs, masseter muscles) and upper airway. Two osteotomy designs (mandibular body DO vs. mandibular angle DO) were simulated to compare condylar stress patterns. Cephalometric and CBCT measurements were applied to assess skeletal, occlusal and TMJ morphological changes. Airway volumetric changes and aerodynamic parameters (velocity, pressure, resistance) at characteristic cross-sections were quantified via CFD. The mandibular body DO concentrated stress on the lateral condylar region, while the mandibular angle DO localized loading on the condylar apex and medioposterior slope. Postoperatively, adaptive condylar remodeling was observed with a 49.15% increase in lateral joint space. The ANB angle decreased by 54.7%, correcting severe skeletal Class II malocclusion to mild with improved facial profile. Total upper airway volume increased by 19.59%, mainly in the velopharynx and glossopharynx. CFD showed markedly reduced airflow velocity and airway resistance after treatment. The mandibular body DO design appeared to achieve a biomechanically favorable condylar stress distribution in simulation, which may promote TMJ stability. Furthermore, moderate CFD-derived improvements in upper airway morphology and aerodynamics were observed; however, without postoperative polysomnography evaluation, these cannot be interpreted as objectively confirmed improvement in OSAHS severity, warranting validation in larger cohorts.
papers.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery

papers.title: Meibomian Gland Development and Maintenance: Mechanisms, Cell States, and Emerging Experimental Models.
papers.abstract: Meibomian glands (MGs) are specialized holocrine sebaceous glands that deliver meibum to the tear-film lipid layer. Classical embryology established the dependence of MG morphogenesis on eyelid closure and fusion, while recent studies have begun to distinguish gland formation from postnatal maintenance. This narrative review examines the mechanisms governing MG development, homeostasis, and dysfunction, together with the experimental models used to study them. Developmental studies place fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling within eyelid morphogenesis and link Wnt modulation and ectodysplasin A signaling to gland formation. Adult mouse genetics and lineage tracing identify KROX20-Notch1 and Hedgehog signaling as regulators of epithelial maintenance. Histone deacetylases regulate progenitor proliferation, survival, and meibocyte differentiation. ABCA12-dependent ductal desquamation supports meibum outflow, while NAD+-dependent circadian steroidogenesis connects local metabolism to gland aging. Single-cell and spatial analyses reveal epithelial states and changes in the glandular microenvironment. Human and mouse organoids recapitulate selected epithelial and lipid-associated features, and early transplantation studies show short-term engraftment. Sustained secretion after transplantation remains a central question for gland replacement. Defects in gland formation, epithelial renewal, local metabolism, or ductal outflow can compromise meibum delivery and contribute to MGD.

papers.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
papers.abstract: Acute total sleep deprivation (SD) produces immediate and severe cognitive impairments. Although propofol has been shown to be effective against cognitive impairments under certain SD circumstances, its pharmacological profile under acute total SD remains to be further explored.
